issues.legal_issue: The challenged preventive powers were constitutionally valid.
material_facts: The petitions challenged the constitutional validity of Section 144 and Chapter VIII of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
In an earlier order in related proceedings, the Court had upheld those provisions as valid and operative.
issues.conclusion: The constitutional challenge failed because the Court had already upheld the provisions in related proceedings.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied its earlier ruling in related proceedings that Section 144 and Chapter VIII of the Code of Criminal Procedure were constitutionally valid and operative.

predicates.constitutional_validity_challenge: A petitioner challenged the constitutionality of preventive powers in a court proceeding.
predicates.same_powers_previously_upheld: The same preventive powers had already been upheld in related proceedings.
predicates.challenged_powers_remain_valid: The challenged preventive powers remain constitutionally valid.

issues.definition: When a constitutional challenge concerns powers already upheld in related proceedings, the challenged powers remain valid.

issues.legal_issue: A general preventive order may be issued when a widespread, unpredictable disturbance makes orders to identified individuals impracticable.
material_facts: A movement to take forcible possession of surplus land was expected to involve an uncertain number of people across the district.
It was not possible to identify in advance who would participate, so individual service of orders was impracticable.
The District Magistrate issued a general order covering the district.
issues.conclusion: The general scope of the order did not exceed the Magistrate’s jurisdiction in the circumstances.
issues.legal_principle: Section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure permits general orders in suitable cases; when the potential participants are numerous and cannot be predetermined, individual orders may not be practicable. The Court also noted that affected persons could represent their case.

predicates.challenge_to_general_preventive_order: A person challenged a general preventive order in a court proceeding.
predicates.widespread_unpredictable_movement: A movement threatened disorder involving an uncertain number of potential participants over a broad area.
predicates.individual_orders_impracticable: The authority could not practicably identify the people who might participate in advance and serve them individually.
predicates.general_order_is_within_jurisdiction: The general preventive order is within the issuing authority’s jurisdiction.

issues.definition: When a general preventive order is challenged and a widespread, unpredictable movement makes individual orders impracticable, the general order is within jurisdiction.

issues.legal_issue: A preventive order is not invalid for want of adequate material or because the authority received government advice when the authority had sufficient information and exercised its own discretion.
material_facts: Reports from people whose lands were targeted described the proposed action clearly and cogently.
The participants’ conduct supported the Magistrate’s apprehension of a real risk of disorder.
The Court found that the District Magistrate had ample material before issuing the order.
The State Government may have advised the District Magistrates on how to respond, but the Court found no basis to conclude that the Magistrate’s discretion had been displaced.
issues.conclusion: The material was sufficient, and any government advice did not amount to an impermissible exercise of the Magistrate’s discretion by the Government.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the Magistrate must have sufficient material to proceed. The Court held that cogent reports and conduct bearing out a real apprehension supplied such material, and that government advice about responding to a general disturbance did not itself transfer the Magistrate’s discretion to the Government.

rule.if: challenge_to_preventive_order and cogent_reports_support_risk and conduct_bears_out_risk and magistrate_exercises_discretion

predicates.challenge_to_preventive_order: A person challenged a preventive order in a court proceeding.
predicates.cogent_reports_support_risk: Reports received by the authority clearly described conduct creating a risk of disorder.
predicates.conduct_bears_out_risk: The conduct of the people involved supported the authority’s apprehension of disorder.
predicates.magistrate_exercises_discretion: The local authority considered the material and made its own decision, even if it had received government advice.
predicates.order_is_supported_by_adequate_material_: The order is supported by adequate material and reflects the local authority’s own discretion.

issues.definition: When a preventive order is challenged, cogent reports and conduct support the apprehended risk, and the local authority exercises its own discretion, the order is supported by adequate material and independent discretion.

issues.legal_issue: A preventive order is valid when its restrictions are necessary and reasonably limited to preventing the apprehended disorder.
material_facts: The order restricted assemblies, processions, demonstrations, weapons, potential missiles, loudspeakers, and forcible possession of land.
The order included exceptions for specified public officials, funeral processions, religious gatherings, and infirm people carrying support sticks.
The Court considered the restrictions necessary in the circumstances and found that they caused the minimum interruption to community life.
The loudspeaker restriction could be relaxed in an appropriate case.
issues.conclusion: The challenged order’s precautionary measures were necessary and sufficiently limited in the circumstances.
issues.legal_principle: Section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure authorizes preventive measures directed at averting the apprehended mischief. The Court considered the restrictions’ purpose, their limited operation, the stated exceptions, and the possibility of relaxing the loudspeaker restriction.

predicates.challenge_to_preventive_order: A person challenged a preventive order in a court proceeding.
predicates.restrictions_address_apprehended_risk: The order’s restrictions were directed at conduct that threatened the apprehended disorder.
predicates.order_has_reasonable_limits: The order limited its effects through appropriate exceptions, limited scope, or a capacity for relaxation where appropriate.

issues.definition: When a challenged preventive order addresses the apprehended risk and has reasonable limits, its restrictions are valid.

issues.legal_issue: Preventive action against people who knowingly persisted in conduct contrary to an operative public-order direction was justified, without resolving the validity of any individual arrest.
material_facts: A prohibitory order had been promulgated and publicized.
The petitioners knew of the order and deliberately defied it.
After being asked to disperse, they persisted in digging the land and placing flags at the site.
The Court stated that the police were entitled to frustrate the attempt by arresting the participants, but expressly did not decide the validity of any particular individual’s arrest.
issues.conclusion: The preventive action was justified for the purposes of the petitions, while the validity of any individual arrest remained for determination on evidence if a trial took place.
issues.legal_principle: The Court treated Section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure as permitting preventive action to avert the threatened disorder and regarded deliberate defiance of a known order as supporting that action. It reserved individual arrest validity for determination on evidence.

rule.if: writ_challenge_to_preventive_action and operative_public_order and person_knows_order and person_persists_in_defiance

predicates.writ_challenge_to_preventive_action: A person challenged preventive action in a writ proceeding.
predicates.operative_public_order: A public-order direction was in force when the conduct occurred.
predicates.person_knows_order: The person knew of the public-order direction.
predicates.person_persists_in_defiance: The person continued the conduct despite being informed of the direction and asked to stop.
predicates.preventive_action_is_justified: The preventive action is justified, without deciding the validity of any individual arrest.

issues.definition: When a person challenges preventive action in a writ proceeding and knowingly persists in defying an operative public-order direction, the preventive action is justified, without deciding the validity of an individual arrest.
